evals.name: zero-touch-one-review-no-linear
evals.prompt:
Auto-post these panel-review findings to PR 90 in catena-labs/web-app (head SHA: c0ffee123). Linear is NOT reachable from this session. Just post the legitimate ones, no triage. Dry run: do NOT call gh api — write the review payload to ./review.json, planned reactions to ./reactions.json, and the disposition report to ./report.md.

Codex (HIGH, security)
- apps/api/src/auth/cookie.ts:30 — Session cookie set without `secure`; the single line `  res.cookie('sid', token, { httpOnly: true })` (2-space indent) should be `  res.cookie('sid', token, { httpOnly: true, secure: true })`. Self-contained one-line replacement.
  Fix: replace that line with `  res.cookie('sid', token, { httpOnly: true, secure: true })`.

Claude (MEDIUM, architecture)
- apps/api/src/services/report.ts:120 — The service formats currency inline instead of using the shared money formatter; should route through the existing `formatMoney` util.
  Fix: use formatMoney(amount) rather than the inline toFixed call.

Claude (LOW, polish)
- apps/api/src/utils/log.ts:8 — Log line omits the request id; the single line `  logger.info(msg)` (2-space indent) should be `  logger.info({ reqId }, msg)`.
  Fix: replace with `  logger.info({ reqId }, msg)`.

All three lines are inside the PR diff. Both code fixes are confident and clearly about this PR's changes.
evals.expected_output: This is ZERO-TOUCH: the skill must NOT call AskUserQuestion at all (no select lists, no confirmation) — it applies the bar automatically and writes the dry-run files. review.json is ONE review payload (an object, NOT a flat array of standalone per-comment payloads): `commit_id: "c0ffee123"` once at the top level, an `event`, a `body`, and a `comments` array of exactly 3 entries, each with `path`, line targeting and `body`. No caller gave an event and the user asked only to post, not for a verdict, so the event is `COMMENT` and the body is exactly `Comments only. No decision.` — a HIGH finding does NOT make this skill request changes by itself. The body has no summary, no finding count and no severity list. Severity is NOT a gate on what posts, so the LOW finding IS in the review. Comment bodies carry NO severity, NO `Recommendation:` line, NO priority, NO panelist attribution. (1) The codex HIGH (cookie.ts:30) is a clean single-line drop-in, so its body MUST carry a ```suggestion block with exactly `  res.cookie('sid', token, { httpOnly: true, secure: true })` (2-space indent), single-line comment anchored to `line: 30`, `side: "RIGHT"`. (2) The claude MEDIUM (report.ts:120) is conceptual/architectural — NOT a faithful drop-in — so its body uses a `**Possible Solution:**` prose line and NO suggestion block. (3) The claude LOW (log.ts:8) is a clean single-line drop-in, so it carries a ```suggestion block with exactly `  logger.info({ reqId }, msg)`, AND because it is LOW/polish its body is prefixed `Small / Optional polish:` (or equivalent). No body has BOTH a suggestion and a prose fix line. Order in `comments` is HIGH→MEDIUM→LOW: cookie.ts (HIGH) first, report.ts (MEDIUM) second, log.ts (LOW) last. reactions.json is an empty array (no existing comments were provided to dedupe against). No linear_tickets.json content is required (Linear unreachable) — if written it must be an empty array. report.md records the PR resolution line (PR #90, resolved from context), the one review and its event (chosen by this skill's rules: no verdict was asked for), all three findings as inline comments (noting suggestion vs prose for each), and that there were no Linear-bound findings.

evals.name: dedupe-thumbs-up-existing-bot-comment-and-request-changes
evals.prompt:
Auto-post these findings to PR 145 in catena-labs/api-service (head SHA: ab99ff1), and request changes if any of them block. Linear not reachable. Dry-run: ./review.json, ./reactions.json, ./report.md — do not call gh api to post, but assume you fetched existing PR comments and found this one already there:

EXISTING inline review comment (from coderabbitai[bot], user.type=Bot) on apps/api/src/charges/refund.ts:42, html_url https://github.com/catena-labs/api-service/pull/145#discussion_r555 , body: "Refund amount isn't validated as positive — a negative value would create a charge."

Findings to act on:

Codex (HIGH, correctness)
- apps/api/src/charges/refund.ts:42 — Refund amount allows negative values, which would create a charge instead of a refund. Validate amount > 0 before processing.
  Fix: guard with `if (amount <= 0) throw new BadRequest('amount must be positive')`.

Codex (MEDIUM, correctness)
- apps/api/src/charges/capture.ts:70 — Capture uses `==` for the status check; should be `===`. The line `  if (charge.status == 'authorized')` should be `  if (charge.status === 'authorized')`.
  Fix: replace with `  if (charge.status === 'authorized')`.

Both lines are in the diff.
evals.expected_output: Zero-touch, no AskUserQuestion. The skill must run the single dedupe pass and recognize the codex HIGH (refund.ts:42) as the SAME issue as the existing coderabbitai[bot] comment (same file, same line, same underlying problem — negative refund amount). So it MUST NOT post a duplicate for that finding: review.json is one review payload (`commit_id: "ab99ff1"`) whose `comments` array contains exactly 1 entry — only the capture.ts:70 MEDIUM. reactions.json contains exactly 1 entry for the refund.ts finding: a planned +1 (`content=+1`) on the existing inline comment, referencing comment surface=inline, the existing html_url (…/pull/145#discussion_r555) and author coderabbitai (a Bot). It must NOT plan a reply to the bot's comment: a reply is a separate comment outside the review. The user asked for a verdict ('request changes if any of them block'), so the event is `REQUEST_CHANGES`: the posted MEDIUM blocks, and the +1'd HIGH counts toward the request too. The body's first line is exactly `This PR needs changes. See the comments.`, followed by one line `Also blocking: https://github.com/catena-labs/api-service/pull/145#discussion_r555` so the author can see every reason for the request. The capture.ts:70 entry is a clean single-line drop-in so its body carries a ```suggestion block with exactly `  if (charge.status === 'authorized')` (2-space indent), anchored to `line: 70`. Neither output dedupes against any human or self comment. report.md records refund.ts as '+1'd existing automated comment (coderabbitai)' and capture.ts as an inline comment (suggestion).

  Fix: replace with `  const taxCents = Math.round(tax)`.

(2) The claude MEDIUM (retry.ts:88) is UNCERTAIN / needs investigation (explicitly can't be confirmed from the diff) → Linear, NOT the PR. So linear_tickets.json has exactly 2 tickets, both with team "Platform", project "Code Health", NO priority field, and descriptions containing the PR link + file:line deep-link, File:, Severity:, then the body, then the fix as a `**Possible Solution:**` prose line (NOT a ```suggestion block, even for cart.ts whose fix is code — suggestions are GitHub-inline-only). evals.name: missing-pr-ref-ambiguous-branch-aborts
evals.prompt:
Auto-post these panel-review findings. No PR number given, and assume `gh pr list --head <current-branch> --state open` returns TWO open PRs for the current branch — the PR is ambiguous. Findings:

Codex (HIGH) - src/a.ts:10 — Null deref on the changed line. Fix: add a guard.
Claude (MEDIUM) - src/b.ts:20 — Missing await. Fix: await the call.

Dry-run: ./review.json, ./report.md.
evals.expected_output: Zero-touch means the skill must NOT prompt for the PR ref (no AskUserQuestion). It also must NOT guess: with no PR ref in context and the open-PR list returning two candidates (count != 1), the guarded auto-detect fails, so the skill MUST ABORT posting. Per the dry-run abort clause, review.json MUST be written as `null` (no review was postable) — not populated with a guessed payload. No payload may be constructed against a guessed PR. report.md must explain that posting was aborted because no PR ref was provided and the branch's open PRs could not be resolved to exactly one (ideally listing the two candidates), and that the user needs to supply a PR number/URL. The skill must use an open-PR LISTING/count check (e.g. `gh pr list --head <branch> --state open`), NOT `gh pr view` (which can't prove the 'exactly one open PR' guard). It must NOT silently fall back to a single PR, must NOT post to either candidate, and must NOT ask a question. (reactions.json and linear_tickets.json need not be written on abort.)

evals.name: line-outside-the-diff-goes-into-the-review-body
evals.prompt:
Auto-post these findings to PR 301 in catena-labs/api-service (head SHA: 51de51de). Linear not reachable. Dry-run: ./review.json, ./reactions.json, ./report.md.

Codex (HIGH, correctness)
- src/billing/invoice.ts:44 — The invoice total is rounded before tax is added, so the total is off by up to one cent. The line `  const total = Math.round(sub) + tax` should be `  const total = Math.round(sub + tax)`.
  Fix: replace with `  const total = Math.round(sub + tax)`.

Claude (MEDIUM, correctness)
- src/billing/ledger.ts:210 — This PR changes what `postEntry` returns, and the caller at this line still reads the old `id` field, so it now reads `undefined`. The line `  const id = entry.id` should be `  const id = entry.entryId`.
  Fix: replace with `  const id = entry.entryId`.

`scripts/pr-diff-lines.sh 301` prints exactly these rows:
src/billing/invoice.ts	40	52
src/billing/ledger.ts	12	30

So invoice.ts:44 is inside the diff, and ledger.ts:210 is NOT (the file is in the PR, but line 210 is outside every hunk). Both findings are confident and about this PR's changes.
evals.expected_output: Zero-touch, no AskUserQuestion. Both findings are confident and in-scope, so both go to the PR, in ONE review. The skill checks each anchor against the rows from `scripts/pr-diff-lines.sh`: invoice.ts:44 is inside the row 40-52, so it is an inline comment; ledger.ts:210 is outside the only ledger.ts row (12-30), so it CANNOT be an inline comment — one such comment would make GitHub reject the whole review with a 422. review.json is one payload: `commit_id: "51de51de"`, `event: "COMMENT"` (nobody asked for a verdict), and `comments` with exactly 1 entry (invoice.ts line 44, a ```suggestion block with exactly `  const total = Math.round(sub + tax)`). The ledger.ts finding is in the review `body`, after the fixed first line `Comments only. No decision.` and a blank line: a `**Location:**` line naming `src/billing/ledger.ts:210` with a blob deep-link at SHA 51de51de, then the finding body verbatim, then the fix as a `**Possible Solution:**` prose line — the suggestion is DOWNGRADED to prose because a suggestion block only works on an inline comment. The finding is NOT dropped, its anchor is NOT moved to a line inside the diff (for example line 30), and it is NOT planned as a separate top-level PR comment. report.md lists invoice.ts as inline (suggestion) and ledger.ts as 'in the review body' with the reason (line outside the diff) and notes the downgrade.

evals.name: caller-event-wins-and-the-approval-carries-the-comments
evals.prompt:
You are the posting step of an auto-review run. The caller (auto-review) hands you: PR 303 in catena-labs/web-app; the pinned reviewed head SHA `77e577e5`; the event `APPROVE`; and the first line of the review body `LGTM, just some small comments, nothing blocking`. Dry-run: ./review.json, ./reactions.json, ./post-report.md (auto-review keeps ./report.md for itself).

Findings from the synthesis:

polish (LOW):
- [LOW] src/format/date.ts:18 — `new Date()` is called twice in one function; read it once. The lines 18-19 `  const start = new Date()\n  const stamp = new Date().toISOString()` should be `  const start = new Date()\n  const stamp = start.toISOString()`.

Lines 18-19 are inside one hunk of the PR diff. The PR head is still `77e577e5` when you fetch it again immediately before the submit.
evals.expected_output: The caller owns the gate, so its event and body line are used as given: the skill does NOT re-derive the event from the findings (its own rules would give `COMMENT` for a LOW-only list) and does NOT refuse `APPROVE`. review.json is one payload: `commit_id: "77e577e5"` — the caller-PINNED SHA, fetched again and confirmed as the head immediately before the submit — `event: "APPROVE"`, a `body` of exactly `LGTM, just some small comments, nothing blocking`, and `comments` with exactly 1 entry: a multi-line comment on src/format/date.ts with `start_line: 18`, `start_side: "RIGHT"`, `line: 19`, `side: "RIGHT"`, a `Small / Optional polish:` prefix, the `[LOW]` tag stripped, and a ```suggestion block with exactly the two replacement lines. The polish comment rides INSIDE the approving review: there is no separate comment review before it, and no standalone comment. The report is written to ./post-report.md, not ./report.md, and it says the caller chose the event. Every SHA in the report and in any deep-link is the pinned `77e577e5`.

evals.name: head-moved-before-the-submit-turns-a-verdict-into-a-comment-review
evals.prompt:
You are the posting step of an auto-review run. The caller (auto-review) hands you: PR 304 in catena-labs/web-app; the pinned reviewed head SHA `aa77aa77`; the event `APPROVE`; the first line of the review body `LGTM`; and its head-moved line `No decision: the head moved during the review. These comments are for aa77aa7.` There are no findings. Dry-run: ./review.json, ./reactions.json, ./post-report.md.

IMPORTANT: when you fetch `headRefOid` again immediately before the submit, it returns `bb88bb88`. The author pushed after the caller decided.
evals.expected_output: The caller's event normally wins, but one limit applies to a caller's event too: before it submits an `APPROVE` or a `REQUEST_CHANGES` review on a pinned commit, the skill fetches the head again, and here the head (`bb88bb88`) is no longer the pinned commit (`aa77aa77`). An approval now would land on a head that nobody reviewed. So the skill does NOT submit `APPROVE`. review.json is one payload: `commit_id: "aa77aa77"` (still the reviewed SHA), `event: "COMMENT"`, a `body` of exactly `No decision: the head moved during the review. These comments are for aa77aa7.` (the caller's head-moved line, verbatim), and no inline comments. The report says plainly that the event changed from the caller's `APPROVE` to `COMMENT` and why, so that the caller reports the verdict that landed and not the one it decided. It must NOT approve, must NOT re-pin the review to `bb88bb88`, and must NOT skip the second head fetch because the caller already checked.
